title: Lantern
description: Explore the checked puncture-capped three-point relation. The boundary-framed lantern relation remains to be encoded.

sections.Surface and conventions: PC means puncture-capped: cap each of the three inner boundaries of the four-holed sphere with a once-marked disk. The lab uses the resulting disk with three marked points. Richard's vertically reflected positive-twist display is the default; braid signs do not change.
sections.Derivation: The three-factor product T12 · T13 · T23 has the same exact B3 action as the direct twist T123. The boundary-framed version needs separate boundary-twist bookkeeping and is not claimed here.
sections.Braid factorization: The lab shows one continuous exact three-strand braid, with blue dotted factor separators and optional compact placement of commuting crossings.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: Each factor uses the shared Arc/Loop surface renderer. The middle column shows the cumulative boundary→1→2→3 cut chain after each factor, with independent arc visibility controls.
sections.Standard mapping classes: The three pairwise Dehn twists and direct three-point boundary twist are encoded as checked marked-disk mapping classes.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: Hurwitz moves, splitting, combining, undo, and save/reopen retain exact disk-action checks. Daisy and boundary-framed lantern substitutions are not encoded.
sections.References: For punctured-disk braid relations, see Margalit and McCammond, Geometric Presentations for the Pure Braid Group (2006).
